dimensions.assessment: Affects large bank holding companies, nonbank financial companies subject to stress tests, the Federal Reserve, and the Government Accountability Office.
dimensions.evidence: nonbank financial companies and large bank holding companies

dimensions.assessment: Changes how capital requirements and stress capital buffers are calculated and publicly disclosed, while banning climate-related stress tests.
dimensions.evidence: The Board may only make material changes to the methodologies established in the rule... through notice and comment rulemaking

dimensions.assessment: Imposes regulatory changes on financial institutions and requires periodic GAO studies, though direct federal spending amounts are not specified.
dimensions.evidence: The Comptroller General of the United States shall, every 3 years, conduct a study and submit a report to the Congress

dimensions.assessment: Requires multiple new administrative rules, restricts the Federal Reserve's testing authorities, and mandates triennial congressional reports.
dimensions.evidence: the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System... shall issue a rule

dimensions.assessment: Imposes permanent rulemaking mandates and ongoing triennial oversight reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: The Comptroller General of the United States shall, every 3 years, conduct a study and submit a report

missing_information: Specific quantitative estimates of compliance cost savings for financial institutions.
Detailed budgetary costs for the GAO reports.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates new Federal Reserve rulemaking regarding bank stress testing models, methodologies, and scenarios, prohibits climate-related stress tests, and requires periodic GAO reports on effectiveness.
